clue.text: It rules 27 in disarray

indicators.note: things in disarray are jumbled out of their proper order, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 27-across, used as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Some ruling body has been thrown into chaos by whatever 27 is.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue and 27-across are anagrams of each other, so solving either one hands you the letters of the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest court in the US hands down rulings, so a cryptic 'it rules' is a playful description of that judicial body.

clue.text: Victory brings legal case against head of sorority housing about 100

indicators.note: a thing housing something holds it inside, so the other letters sit within

parts.note: to sue is to bring a legal case
C is short for circa, Latin for about
C is the Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: 'head of' keeps only the first letter of 'sorority'

parts.note: the first letter of sorority

explanation.surface: A sorority's head, accused of overcrowding the house, faces a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: The word that brings the case houses the two Cs and then stands against, that is next to, the sorority's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Success is achieving what you aimed for, and a victory is a success in a contest.

clue.text: Pleads with outspoken flattery

indicators.note: outspoken here means spoken out, so the word is said rather than spelt

parts.note: flattery is praise, and that word sounds the same as the answer

explanation.surface: Someone begs for favour by being frank in their flattery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outspoken' normally means blunt, but read as 'spoken out' it signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To pray in the old sense is to beseech or entreat, so one who prays pleads.

clue.text: With nothing 23, roles can be distributed up to three times

parts.words: roles can be distributed up to three times
parts.note: surface reading: parts in a play may be handed out in as many as three rounds

parts.words: roles can be distributed up to three times
parts.note: setter's reading: the answer is spelt only from the letters of roles, each letter used up to three times

explanation.surface: Casting goes smoothly when parts are handed out in a few rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 23-down means wrong, so the definition asks for a word meaning flawless. The second half is a letter puzzle: R appears three times, E and S twice, O and L once.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with nothing amiss contains no mistakes at all, so it is free of any slip or fault.

clue.text: Raising stake for mount

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: an ante is a poker stake

explanation.surface: Upping the bet to buy a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a horse to ride, but it is the short form of mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is a volcano in Sicily, and mount is the title for a mountain.

clue.text: Amounts to more than passé songs

parts.note: out means out of fashion, passé
numbers are songs in a show or set

explanation.surface: These songs are worth more than old-fashioned ones.
explanation.definitionFit: To outnumber a group is to exceed it in quantity, being greater in count.

clue.text: Henri, swimming in a river

indicators.note: swimming letters move about freely, so they settle in a new order

parts.note: letters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Henri, one of the two setters, is out swimming in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine is a major European river flowing from the Swiss Alps to the North Sea.

clue.text: Synagogue member, leading Central American country, announced anniversary celebrations

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so the first piece comes before the second
announced means spoken aloud, so the words count for their sound, not their spelling

parts.note: a member of a synagogue is a Jew
Belize is a small country in Central America

explanation.surface: A synagogue member at the head of a Central American state declares national anniversary festivities.
explanation.definitionFit: Jubilees are celebrations marking significant anniversaries, such as a monarch's 25th or 50th year.

clue.text: Say hi again, without energy or remorse

indicators.note: without means lacking, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: to greet once more
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Greeting someone a second time, but listlessly and without any sense of guilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Regret is sorrow over something done, much the same as remorse.

clue.text: Mostly, talk and smile in embarrassment

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to chat is to talk
a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: Someone mumbles and grins sheepishly because they feel awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is a feeling of vexed humiliation, a close synonym of embarrassment.

clue.text: Massachusetts college included in clichéd testimonial

indicators.note: one thing included in another sits inside it, so these letters go within the other word

parts.note: trite means overused, hackneyed
BU is Boston University

explanation.surface: A college's name turns up inside a stale, formulaic letter of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: BU stands for Boston University, which is in Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribute is an expression of praise or esteem, much like a testimonial honouring someone.

clue.text: Result involves reverse guarantee

indicators.note: to involve is to take in or include, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: to ensue is to follow as a result
R is the standard abbreviation for reverse, as on a gear stick

explanation.surface: An outcome that includes some kind of backward warranty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' looks like an instruction to turn something round, but here it simply stands for its abbreviation R.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure something is to make certain of it, which is what to guarantee means as a verb.

clue.text: In the end, toss our ripe bananas in a lake

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, which is the one kept here

parts.note: the last letter of toss

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

parts.note: letters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone flings overripe bananas into a lake at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like the fruit being tossed, but it is the slang word for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Superior is the largest of the North American Great Lakes, so the name is an example of a lake.

clue.text: Conclusion of agreement with Santa's staff overturned favorite type of recovery program

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter, which is the one kept

parts.note: the last letter of agreement
W is a standard abbreviation for with
Santa's workshop is staffed by elves

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned means flipped upside down, so the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Santa's helpers have overturned a deal over which recovery program is the favorite.
explanation.walkthrough: Twelve-step programs, such as Alcoholics Anonymous, guide addicts through a series of stages; 'with' looks like a link word but supplies a letter, and 'favorite' is wordplay, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve-step describes a style of addiction recovery program built on a fixed sequence of principles.

clue.text: Birds weep bitterly in a trap

indicators.note: something done bitterly is done in anguish and turmoil, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: letters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Birds caught in a snare are crying in distress.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider spins its web precisely to catch flying insects, so it serves as a snare.

clue.text: "Ego" is Latin translation for JK or HP

parts.note: ego is the Latin word for I, the first-person pronoun

indicators.note: translating turns words into new forms, so the letters are reworked into a different arrangement

parts.note: letters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A note on Latin: ego is the word for I, and here is how it translates for two people.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a Latin lesson, but 'translation' tells you to shuffle 'is Latin'; ego simply gives I. JK and HP could be J. K. Rowling or the setters' own names.
explanation.definitionFit: JK and HP are pairs of letters standing for someone's first and last names, which is what initials are.

clue.text: Build terminals in advance for large Quebec airport

indicators.note: terminals are end points, so only the closing letter of each word is taken

parts.note: the final letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: A plan to construct new terminal buildings ahead of time for a big Quebec airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terminals' looks like airport buildings, which suits the surface perfectly, but it means the end letters of the following words.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect a structure is to put it up, the same as to construct or build it.

clue.text: Carol eats all over the place — that's one way to move up

indicators.note: something all over the place is scattered and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: letters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Carol is a messy eater who gets food everywhere, and somehow that is how she rises in the world.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving staircase carries people from one floor to a higher one, so it is a means of going up.

clue.text: Clay's new name, for instance!

parts.note: the boxer Cassius Clay changed his name to Muhammad Ali
as means for instance, as in 'cities such as Paris'

explanation.surface: The boxer's adopted name is offered as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: Muhammad Ali's name was itself an assumed name replacing Cassius Clay.
explanation.definitionFit: An alias is an assumed name used in place of the original, exactly what Ali was for Clay.

clue.text: Have an influence on law featuring fluorine and iron

indicators.note: a thing featuring something includes it within itself, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: an act is a law passed by a legislature
F is the chemical symbol for fluorine
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A statute containing chemicals could sway public health.
explanation.definitionFit: To affect something is to produce a change in it, the same as having an influence upon it.

clue.text: I cry uncontrollably, absorbed by catalogs for some songwriters

indicators.note: what is absorbed by something ends up inside it

parts.note: a catalog is a list

indicators.note: doing something uncontrollably means without order, so the letters spill out rearranged

parts.note: letters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone weeps helplessly while poring over songwriting catalogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyricists write the words of songs, so they are a kind of songwriter, hence 'some'.

clue.text: Mark lies about unfinished embrace with professor

indicators.note: to lie about something is to surround it, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin

indicators.note: an unfinished word is missing its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to hold someone is to embrace them

explanation.surface: Mark tells untruths about an interrupted hug with a professor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' reads as a man's name, but it is the ordinary noun; 'lies' is not about untruths but about position.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned academic, and a professor is a prime example of one.

clue.text: Scare 3 in marsh

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, so the first piece is set within the second

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land
3-down is ERRORLESS, which means correct

explanation.surface: A cross-reference turns up in a marsh to give someone a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: The number 3 means 'the answer to 3-down', and you need a synonym of it, not the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To frighten someone is to make them afraid, the same as to scare them.

clue.text: TV host standing up for comedian

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means reading from the bottom to the top

parts.note: Oprah Winfrey hosted a famous TV talk show

explanation.surface: A television host stands in for a comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing up' suggests stand-up comedy, which fits the surface, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Harpo was one of the Marx Brothers, the silent comic who played the harp.

clue.text: Make white line in the sand

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, so the first piece is set within the second

parts.note: a beach is the sand at the shore
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone paints a white boundary line in the sand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line in the sand' is a familiar idiom for a firm limit, which hides that line is just L inside a word for sand.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleach something is to remove its colour with chemicals, whitening it.

clue.text: A young woman is wrong

parts.note: taken as written
miss is a title for a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A young woman has made a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amiss is out of order or faulty, so it is wrong.

clue.text: Ultimate implement for a shoemaker

definitions.meaning: first meaning: final, coming at the end
second meaning: a foot-shaped block on which shoes are made

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the best tool a cobbler could own; the two halves are unrelated senses of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means final as an adjective and is also the foot-shaped wooden form cobblers use to shape footwear.

clue.text: One is guilty of thrusting Mexican politicians into sect

indicators.note: thrusting something into another means pushing it inside, so the party goes within

parts.note: a cult is a sect
the PRI is Mexico's Institutional Revolutionary Party

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of pushing Mexican politicians into a religious sect.
explanation.definitionFit: A culprit is the person responsible for a wrong, the one who is guilty of it.

clue.text: An exciting sensation: dropping right in where bugs live

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: dropping something lets it fall away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a thrill is an exciting sensation
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A buzz of excitement gets lost on the way to where insects are found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bugs' is casual American usage for insects, which include ants.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthill is the mound colony where ants live, and ants are insects, informally bugs.

clue.text: Surfer, perhaps, is reckless 1A

indicators.note: reckless behaviour is wild and disorderly, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: the answer to 1-across, used as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A surfer is accused of being as rash as whatever 1-across is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surfer' suggests waves, but it means someone surfing the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who surfs the web browses online sites, so a web surfer is an example of one who uses a computer.
